content:
Dutch developer Jordi Bruin rolled out an update to his excellent transcription app MacWhisper this week with a much-requested feature: the ability to automatically identify previously named speakers in new recordings. Here are the details.

MacWhisper just keeps getting better

I’ve written multiple times in the past couple of years about how MacWhisper has become an integral part of my podcast post-production workflow for show notes, episode descriptions, and more.

Which is why I’ve followed the app’s development very closely, and Jordi’s efforts to make it an increasingly powerful tool for casual and power users alike.

In the last few months alone, MacWhisper got a completely redesigned transcript editor, real-time meeting transcription, significantly improved speaker detection, deeper integration with Apple Intelligence, Siri, and Spotlight, and support for multiple new transcription models.

This week, MacWhisper got updated to version 16, packing several improvements, chief among them the ability to recognize speakers based on their voices in previous transcripts.

Until now, while MacWhisper could distinguish between different speakers in a recording (a process known as speaker diarization), users still had to assign names to each new transcription manually. With MacWhisper 16, that is no longer necessarily the case.

Now, MacWhisper creates a set of voiceprints for the speakers users have previously identified, and uses them as a reference when processing new recordings. Depending on the confidence level of a match, MacWhisper will either automatically assign the speaker’s name or ask the user to confirm their identity.

According to Bruin, as users transcribe more recordings featuring the same people, MacWhisper gets better at recognizing their voices. All voiceprint processing and storage happen on-device, which is a great touch.

The feature also works with existing transcripts, which is fantastic for longtime MacWhisper users such as myself. A new Voice Recognition section in the app’s settings lets users generate voiceprints from existing transcripts, clear a speaker’s stored voice data, or turn the feature off altogether.

Importantly, voice recognition also works with live meeting transcriptions, although automatic name assignments happen once the meeting ends.

The new feature requires a MacWhisper Pro license, an Apple silicon Mac, and on-device transcription with speaker detection enabled.

Here are the full release notes for MacWhisper 16:

New

  • Voice Recognition: Name a speaker once and MacWhisper recognizes their voice in the transcriptions you make after that. Recognized people are marked “Named by voice match” in the transcript’s People list, where you can confirm or correct them. Requires an Apple silicon Mac and on-device transcription with speaker detection. (Pro)
  • Voice Recognition: When a live meeting ends, MacWhisper names the people whose voices it recognizes. Anyone you named during the meeting keeps that name. (Pro)
  • Voice Recognition: Settings > People has a new Voice Recognition section, where you can turn recognition off, learn voices from your existing transcripts, and forget a person’s voice. (Pro)

    • Improved

    • Live meetings: The meeting window has a new look. (Pro)
    • Live meetings: The meeting window now stays above other apps, with a pin button to turn that off. (Pro)
    • Live meetings: Click a speaker’s name to rename them. MacWhisper now suggests people you have created in the past, both as you type and in the speaker’s menu. (Pro)
    • Live meetings: If you name your own microphone during a meeting and Your Name is not set, MacWhisper remembers it for the next meeting. (Pro)
    • Live meetings: The window now says when the model is still loading and that the meeting is already being recorded, instead of showing Listening. (Pro)

      • Fixed

      • Fixed: On a Mac whose login items service does not respond, MacWhisper could freeze while opening, with no window.
      • Fixed: In a live meeting, a speaker’s right-click menu closed by itself while people were talking. (Pro)
      • Fixed: Typing a new name over the person picked as Your Name no longer renames or removes that person. (Pro)
